title: Provenance for every field
statement: Record where each field came from, not only each record, marking model-inferred content as unsourced with its reasoning, because one record can mix official text with generated fields.
example: In one course's 2,703 records, 43% had at least one generated field.
detail: An audit of an AP curriculum store found records under one source tag whose statements were official but whose misconceptions and assessment boundaries had been filled in by a model, because the official framework doesn't publish them (`icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/feedback_field_level_provenance.md`, lines 12-21). Field-level tags were then added: in one course 43% of 2,703 records had a generated field, mostly dates and themes, with misconceptions, boundaries or objectives generated in 88 (3%) (line 29). It takes recording where every asset came from down to each field.
against: Generated fields were few, and they were kept as a lower tier rather than dropped: "- For the LLM-tagged remainder (3%/1%): use as inspiration only, IB-graded as truth-checker" (`icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/feedback_field_level_provenance.md`, line 33). In the other course 77% of records had a generated field, mostly dates and themes (line 30). For the main course, model-written misconceptions, scope boundaries and objectives were few, 88 records or 3% (`feedback_field_level_provenance.md`, line 29), and no harm from mixed records was measured. Mostly absent in practice: 'Most existing data was loaded from Google Sheets without per-field citations. Requiring `sources` across the board would fail validation on ~20,000 existing files.' (shadow-curriculum/plans/schema-decisions.md line 92).

evidence.quote: When a corpus marks provenance at the record level (e.g., `merge_source: inceptbench_remapped`), do **NOT** treat all fields in that record as equally authoritative. Different fields in the same record can have different provenance. A consumer that trains on the record as a unit will train on the LLM-generated fields as if they were authoritative.
The CB CED does not publish assessment_boundaries or common_misconceptions for APEURO; null fields were filled by Haiku-4.5. Record-level merge_source masks this from consumers.
- APUSH (2,703 records): 43% have any LLM-tagged field. **Misconceptions/boundaries/LOs LLM-filled in only 88 records (3%).** date+theme are the dominant LLM-backfill targets.
- For the LLM-tagged remainder (3%/1%): use as inspiration only, IB-graded as truth-checker
- APWH (1,696 records): 77% have any LLM-tagged field. **Misconceptions/boundaries/LOs LLM-filled in only 23 records (1%).** date+theme dominate.
Curriculum API merge_source is record-level; same record mixes CB-canonical statement with Haiku-generated misconceptions/assessment_boundaries.
The `statement` field carries CB-canonical KC text. The `common_misconceptions` and `assessment_boundaries` fields carry Haiku-4.5-generated text
APUSH (2,703 records): 43% have any LLM-tagged field.
- Filter `'common_misconceptions' NOT IN (llm_generated_fields or [])` → 97% of APUSH, 99% of APWH misconceptions are CB-canonical, safe as authoritative distractor seeds
| Curriculum dataset | Had LLM-fabricated fields (APEURO assessment_boundaries, common_misconceptions, expanded_LOs all Haiku-generated) |
every text field in any new corpus must trace to a primary source; LLMs are tools (search/OCR/reformat) not content authors; drop-don't-patch when sources fail.

- `source` must be nullable because some content is LLM-inferred and has no external citation — but the rationale for that inference is still valuable audit data, so `reasoning` stays required. ("We made this up, and here's why" is more useful than "we made this up.")
**Decision:** `sources` is an object whose keys are free-form — typically the name of the field each citation backs, or the string `"this"` for the entity as a whole.
a flat array forces that mapping to live in prose inside `reasoning`, where it can drift.
"reasoning": "Inferred by LLM (Gemini 2.5 Pro) using the CB Assessment Framework PDF as context — no CB source explicitly defines key concepts at the per-standard level."
Contract consumes a versioned cue/spec artifact and records timing provenance
You invent only what no input specifies, and everything you invent you list in `_gates.invented` so a reviewer can see it.
